extracted.intended_audience: photojournalists and photographers (amateur and professional) preparing submissions for the Pictures of the Year International competition
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and quality criteria for submitting photographs, picture stories, portfolios, editing and documentary entries to the Pictures of the Year International (POY) contest. Covers eligibility, technical file specs, ethical standards, caption/IPTC requirements, category limits, and judging expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry eligibility dates / publication window
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries must be created or published for the first time between Jan. 1 and Dec. 31, 2025.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To accommodate pictures/stories created in 2024 but first published in 2025, Picter will accept images created in 2024 only if first-published by a 3rd party media organization in 2025. Personal websites or social media do not qualify as first publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: First-time publication definition
rubrics_metrics.description: First-time publication is defined as being published by a 3rd party media organization in print or online.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personal web sites or social media accounts do not qualify as first publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpublished picture-story date mix allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: For unpublished picture stories, at least 60% of the pictures must have been photographed in 2025.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You are allowed to include up to 40% (or up to 4 pictures) from previous years. These standards apply to all categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: POY acceptance / rejection and review practice
rubrics_metrics.description: POY may reject any entry that does not meet the standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: POY reviews submissions in advance of judging and often contacts photographers for clarification; note that notice may not be given if an entry is not accepted. Once judging begins, judges may disqualify an entry if it does not meet POY standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may enter
rubrics_metrics.description: POY is open to amateur and professional photographers; entrants may be independent or affiliated with media organizations, NGOs, or specialty advocacy organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entrants may be independent or affiliated with newspapers, magazines, photo agencies, media companies, NGOs, or specialty advocacy organizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total entries per person
rubrics_metrics.description: A maximum of 15 entries can be entered in any combination of categories per person.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category-specific entry limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Limits on number of entries per category type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Up to 10 entries in single image and picture story categories; up to 5 entries in online editing and documentary categories; up to 7 entries in newspaper and magazine editing categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of one entry
rubrics_metrics.description: What constitutes a single entry depends on category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One picture in a single-picture category; one picture story (5-12 photographs); one project (12-40 photographs) in a premiere category; one portfolio in Photographer or Visual Editor of the Year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category selection and movement
rubrics_metrics.description: The jury may judge an entry based on how well it meets the category definition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider your category decision carefully; judges may not move an entry to a new category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photographer credit rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Photographs will be credited to individual photographers for single images and picture stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Team credits for single images and picture stories are not allowed. A single photograph may be submitted only once among the single-picture categories, but a single photograph may be entered in a single image category and also as part of a picture story, a portfolio, and one premiere category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Picture story length and uniqueness
rubrics_metrics.description: A picture story equals 5-12 photos.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not submit multiple versions of the same story. Picture story entries should have a clearly defined structure; each image should contribute unique information. In final rounds judges focus on the quality of the edit; eliminate weak and redundant images.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence preservation for picture stories
rubrics_metrics.description: The sequence of images you create will be preserved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can change the sequence after you upload the images. POY cannot change the sequence of your images.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portfolio title slide requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: For portfolio categories (#25,#26,#27), create a title slide with specific visual and metadata requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Title slide: white text on black background. Put the title and story summary in the IPTC title and caption fields. Place the slide at the beginning of each story.

rubrics_metrics.name: File type and basic photo technical specs
rubrics_metrics.description: Photo file type and minimum size/resolution requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File type: .JPG. Image Size: 3,000 pixels minimum on the longer side. Resolution: 300 dpi minimum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Print editing file submission rules
rubrics_metrics.description: How to submit print editing entries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cannot accept .pdf files — convert to .jpg files. Submit each page as a separate .jpg file. A double truck (two facing pages) should be submitted as a single .jpg file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Video and website entry submission method
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not upload video files for web or video entries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit a .jpg thumbnail image and an active URL for each video and online entry. Include required usernames and passwords. Video files from all winning entries will be provided to POY.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required IPTC metadata fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Required embedded IPTC fields that must be present in images.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embed metadata so Picter fields populate automatically. Required IPTC fields: Document Title (image title), Author (photographer's name), Description (caption), Location Information (city or nearest city, state/province, country), Capture Date (verify the date; images outside eligible date range may be rejected). IPTC can be embedded using Photo Mechanic, Adobe Photoshop, Lightroom, or Bridge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caption content and language rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Captions must meet journalistic standards for accuracy and be ready for publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a date in each caption even if the exact date is unknown (e.g., 'The photo was taken in February 2025'). Do not include your name or organization in the caption. Submit all captions in English. Captions are read in the final rounds — well-written, concise captions with relevant details strengthen your entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics — accurate representation / no staging
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries should be accurate representations of a news scene or candid moment; do not set up or stage photographs (only portraits may be posed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: POY follows the NPPA Code of Ethics; all captions and story summaries should meet journalistic standards for accuracy and publication requirements. Link provided to NPPA code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on AI-generated or manipulated images
rubrics_metrics.description: POY does not accept AI-generated or manipulated images in any category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not add or remove content from your images. Entries must not be digitally manipulated or altered through post-production processing that adds, alters, or removes elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable post-production
rubrics_metrics.description: Routine post-production processing is allowed but excessive manipulation is not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Routine corrections for exposure, white balance, and color toning are acceptable. Excessive saturation or desaturation, flagrant pre- or post-production effects using excessive tonal aberrations, textures, vignettes, color saturation, or other manipulations may be disqualified. Heavily edited images can repel judges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Black & white image standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for black & white images.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Black & white images should be bi-tonal and display a full grayscale range of 256 intensities from black to white. Black & white files that artificially impose a color shift (such as sepia or cyan tones) may be disqualified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disallowed formats and effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific items not allowed in entries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diptychs and triptychs are not allowed. Digitally manufactured photo illustrations, masks, borders, backgrounds, text, handwritten notes, or other effects are prohibited. Film edges are allowed only if the original was shot on film/Polaroid and the border is true to the medium.

rubrics_metrics.name: Smartphone image allowance and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Smartphone images are permitted but with restrictions on filters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Smartphone images are allowed; however, filters that apply excessive tonal aberrations, textures, vignettes, or other manipulations are not allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on subject/employer/conflicted access
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries are not accepted when the subject is also the employer or when access was restricted to hired photographers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Business promotions, catalogs, branded content, or stories in which the funding organization is also the primary subject are not allowed. You may not submit entries that feature your employer. For example, a team photographer cannot enter images of the team that employs them. POY does not accept images and stories from government agencies or state‑sponsored media that do not practice editorial independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original files and additional images on request
rubrics_metrics.description: POY may request originals for verification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: POY may request the original RAW or JPG image files, plus any images that the jury requests. Any photograph that does not meet POY standards may be disqualified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editing (design/presentation) judging criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: How editing categories are evaluated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editing categories recognize excellence in presentation of visual journalism in print and online formats. Design should reflect effectiveness of how story elements contribute to visual storytelling and respect the vision of the photographer. Criteria may consider how photojournalistic aspects are supported by design, display typography, captions, graphics, animation, and interactive elements. Editors are encouraged to use the description field to describe their role in reporting and presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentary category definition and judging criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition and standards for documentary (video) entries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documentary is defined as a non-fiction, video narrative relying on visual reporting of real situations/people, following observational and direct cinema techniques and strict journalistic ethics. Judging appraises storytelling, editing decisions, news judgement, visual aesthetics, audio, and narrative structure. Documentaries must be published/shared publicly via broadcast or festivals during 2025; content from previous years may be included but documentaries entered in previous years are not allowed. Entries should be presented in a web-based linear format that plays start-to-finish; fictional stories, staged reenactments, docudramas, or TV news reports where an anchor tells the story are not allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry fee payment and Picter workflow
rubrics_metrics.description: How to pay and register entries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pay the entry fee at https://poy.org. Fee is US$50 (rises to US$60 on Jan. 6). Receive a reference code in your receipt, then enter the code at Picter and enter POY.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caption writing tips (ENTRY TIPs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical tips on writing effective captions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each caption should include a date even if the specific date is unknown. Short, concise captions are often more effective than long captions. The focus of POY is storytelling ability of the images; not all captions are read in their entirety. Well-written captions with relevant details strengthen your entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Picture story and portfolio editing guidance (ENTRY TIPs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical guidance for constructing picture stories and portfolios.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Picture story entries should have a clearly defined structure; each image should contribute unique information. In final rounds judges often focus on the quality of the edit; eliminate weak and redundant images. For portfolios, the title slide provides important context—keep the title short—and individual captions can expand story details. Single images may not be repeated in a picture story in the same portfolio.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency about creative techniques
rubrics_metrics.description: Be transparent about legitimate creative techniques used to make an image.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Including a description of your technique in the caption field can increase judges' appreciation for your effort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judging transparency practice
rubrics_metrics.description: POY livestreams judging to promote transparency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The competition livestreams judges' discussions and shares schedule/details at www.poy.org so the public can see juried discussions.
